discovery: Weak measurement and weak values (the time-symmetric two-state vector formalism of quantum measurement)

nominees.name: Yakir Aharonov
nominees.affiliation: Chapman University, USA, and Tel Aviv University, Israel

motivation: In 1988 Aharonov, Albert and Vaidman showed that weakly coupling a meter to a pre- and post-selected quantum system yields a well-defined 'weak value', which can lie far outside the eigenvalue spectrum. Building on the time-symmetric two-state vector formalism of Aharonov and Vaidman, this concept turned questions long dismissed as meaningless, such as what a particle does between preparation and detection, into operational measurements. Laboratories worldwide have since used weak values to observe average photon trajectories, resolve Hardy's paradox, directly measure wavefunctions, and amplify tiny signals, achieving record sensitivity in beam-deflection and spin-Hall measurements. Weak values are now linked to contextuality and quantum metrology. The idea changed how physicists reason about measurement, causality and time in quantum mechanics, and it created an experimental toolkit used across quantum optics. Aharonov's lifetime of foundational insight, including the Aharonov-Bohm effect, further underscores this nomination.
